m1.title: Scan this device’s code with a remote that is already paired
m1.when: For when you already have a paired phone or browser. The quickest way; no need to touch the Agent J host.
m1.s1: On the phone that is already paired, open Agent J and tap the scan icon at the top right.
m1.s2: Scan the code below with it.
m1.s3: Both devices show the same 6 digits. If they match, tap “They match — add it” on that phone. No passphrase to type.

m2.title: Run `agentj pair` in the Agent J host’s terminal
m2.when: For your first pairing, or when no paired remote is at hand. Works for everyone.
m2.s1: On the Agent J host, open a terminal and run the command below. A QR code appears in the terminal.
m2.s1ios: On the Agent J host, open a terminal and run the command below. It prints a pairing link that starts with https://.
m2.where: Where the terminal is: on macOS open Terminal; on Windows open PowerShell or Windows Terminal; on Linux open your terminal app.
m2.s2: On this device, tap Scan QR code below and point it at the code in the terminal. A phone can also use its own camera app.
m2.s2ios: Get that link onto this iPhone (AirDrop, or send it to yourself), copy it, paste it into the link box below and tap Pair.
m2.s3: This device shows a 6-digit safety code: type it into the terminal on the Agent J host and press Enter; if you set an approval passphrase, type that too.
m2.alt: Run this command in the Agent J host’s terminal; it prints a pairing link that starts with https://. Copy it onto this device, paste it below, then tap Pair.

m3.title: Add it in the account dashboard
m3.when: For computers already in an Agent J account. No terminal; you confirm with your passkey.
m3.s1: In a browser on another device (the Agent J host, say), open the account dashboard, find the seat card of the Agent J host you want, and tap “Add a remote (phone or browser)”.
m3.s2: Confirm with your passkey. A QR code appears in the account dashboard.
m3.s3: On this device, tap Scan QR code below and scan it. That’s it, no code to type. Or copy the link in the account dashboard and paste it into the link box above.

ar.navNote: the Agent J host's AI got signed out? Sign it in again from the phone.
ar.intro: When the Claude Code / Codex subscription login on the Agent J host expires, the Agent cannot reply. Tap Sign in again here: the Agent J host runs the official login command and sends its authorize link or device code to the phone; you approve on any device signed in to that account, and the new credential stays on the Agent J host. the Agent J host then restarts the AI, checks it is not stuck on any confirmation screen and sends a test message — only a reply shows Recovered.
ar.introBalance: If it is only out of balance or quota, top up on the provider's site — no new sign-in needed.
ar.safety: Starting a rescue needs the owner's passkey. Codes and tokens go only into the secret card, end-to-end encrypted to the Agent J host — never into chat, logs or the relay.

Paste an existing token: run `claude setup-token` on any computer with Claude Code and paste the token into the secret card. Both are live-checked before they are saved.
ar.claudeCNote: Same as /login at the Agent J host: the credential goes to ~/.claude/.credentials.json and renews itself; the Claude windows you open on the Agent J host use it too.
ar.codexNote: the Agent J host runs the official `codex login --device-auth` and shows a link and a one-time code; open the link on any device that can sign in to your ChatGPT account and enter the code — nothing to paste back.
